$schema_notes: One entry per font. `fontsource` is the npm package id to bundle (variable packages are named @fontsource-variable/<id>; static packages are @fontsource/<id>). `category` is one of ui-sans | display | document-serif | monospace — the four spreads the brief asked for. `license` was read from api.fontsource.org/v1/fonts/<id> on 2026-09-24 (fontsource mirrors the font's own OFL.txt from the Google Fonts repo); every entry here came back OFL-1.1 — none needed the Apache-2.0 fallback. `weights` is the full weight list the family ships (not every weight need be loaded by a consumer). `description` and `avoid_for` are this designer's own words, written after reading each font's own specimen page and (for the 15 in pairings.json) after rendering it.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.description: A neutral, high-x-height grotesque built for screens; tight spacing and even strokes keep 13-16px UI text crisp on light and dark backgrounds alike. Already our own body face app-wide — steady rather than characterful.
fonts.avoid_for: Display headlines or a wordmark — excluded from this library as a display choice by the brief itself, since at large size it reads as the generic 'AI product' default.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Sans
fonts.description: A humanist sans with slightly squared curves and an engineered, technical feel (IBM's corporate face); clear at small UI sizes with a little more personality than Inter, though its numerals run wider.
fonts.avoid_for: Dense tabular numbers — the wider figures cost horizontal space in a tight column.

fonts.name: Work Sans
fonts.description: An open, screen-optimized grotesque with a generous x-height; friendly and slightly rounded without being cute, holds up well as 13px body copy.
fonts.avoid_for: Very tight, dense data grids — its open spacing wants room to breathe.

fonts.name: Public Sans
fonts.description: USWDS's civic-service sans — plain, sturdy, unpretentious, built for forms and long-form reading; institutional in a reassuring way, not a corporate-brand way.
fonts.avoid_for: Any moment the product wants to feel playful or expressive — it reads deliberately plain by design.

fonts.name: Manrope
fonts.description: A geometric-leaning sans with softly trimmed corners; modern and a little warm, a good body face under an expressive display heading.
fonts.avoid_for: Anywhere italic emphasis is needed — no italic style ships; use weight for emphasis instead.

fonts.name: Karla
fonts.description: A grotesque with a few quiet quirks (a two-story 'a', slightly springy curves); calm at UI sizes, a notch friendlier than a pure neutral grotesque without tipping into 'rounded app' territory.
fonts.avoid_for: Numerals-heavy dashboards — figures are proportional by default and can misalign in a table unless tabular-nums is forced.

fonts.name: Figtree
fonts.description: A rounded-corner grotesque, friendly and a little soft, common in consumer product UI; reads warm at UI sizes without reading like a children's app.
fonts.avoid_for: A face that must feel serious or institutional (finance-adjacent, legal-adjacent copy) — its warmth works against gravity there.

fonts.name: Plus Jakarta Sans
fonts.description: A geometric sans with slightly condensed proportions and confident, even strokes; reads more 'designed' than Inter at small sizes, good for product-marketing UI.
fonts.avoid_for: Long paragraphs of body text — the condensed rhythm gets tiring past a few sentences.

fonts.name: Atkinson Hyperlegible
fonts.description: Designed by the Braille Institute to disambiguate easily-confused letterforms (1/l/I, O/0); unusual proportions at display size but unmatched clarity at small UI sizes for low-vision readers.
fonts.avoid_for: Headings or marketing — its distinguishing shapes (open counters, an unusual 'l') read as unpolished at large sizes, and only two weights ship.

fonts.name: Fraunces
fonts.description: A warm, old-style display serif with soft, ink-trap-like curves; already our own heading face for the wordmark and verdict tiers — characterful without going decorative, and it holds a large size well.
fonts.avoid_for: Body copy or small UI labels — its low-contrast strokes were drawn for headline sizes, not 13px.

fonts.name: Newsreader
fonts.description: An editorial, book-like serif in the Georgia/Times lineage but drawn softer; reads calm and 'written by a person' at headline size, and stays legible enough to carry a short article body too.
fonts.avoid_for: A punchy, high-energy brand moment — it reads measured, not loud.

fonts.name: Playfair Display
fonts.description: A high-contrast Didone serif — thin hairlines against heavy stems — dramatic and editorial-magazine at large size.
fonts.avoid_for: Small sizes or busy backgrounds — the hairlines can thin out or vibrate below about 24px, and it's an overused 'elegant AI brand' default if not paired deliberately.

fonts.name: DM Serif Display
fonts.description: A calm, moderate-contrast serif display face, closer to a transitional book serif than Playfair's drama; reads warm and confident at headline size with just the one weight to lean on.
fonts.avoid_for: Any UI needing a bold or black display weight, or body text — ships regular only, drawn for short headlines.

fonts.name: Instrument Serif
fonts.description: A quiet, slightly compressed serif with a distinctive italic; closer to a typewriter-adjacent book face than a grand display serif — understated rather than dramatic.
fonts.avoid_for: Long headlines — its compressed rhythm was drawn for a short, quiet phrase, not multi-line hero copy.

fonts.name: Young Serif
fonts.description: A quirky, slightly rounded slab-leaning serif with warm, hand-set character; playful without being a script face.
fonts.avoid_for: Anything that needs to read serious or authoritative (a verdict card, money) — its playfulness undercuts gravity there.

fonts.name: Bricolage Grotesque
fonts.description: A contemporary grotesque with a built-in optical-size axis — tightens and gets quirkier at display sizes, settles down for text; distinctive without being a novelty face.
fonts.avoid_for: Body copy set at its most expressive optical setting — dial the axis back or it reads noisy below headline size.

fonts.name: Archivo
fonts.description: A grotesque built for posters and headlines — even, confident, a little industrial; the heavy weights carry real authority for a verdict tier or a marketing headline.
fonts.avoid_for: Light weights as long-form body text — 400 reads flat in a paragraph; save it for the heavier headline weights it was designed for.

fonts.name: Unbounded
fonts.description: A wide, geometric display face with a distinct rounded-square rhythm; reads bold and 'product launch' at headline size, closer to a wordmark face than a workhorse heading.
fonts.avoid_for: Anything longer than a very short headline or logotype — its width and quirks make it hard to read in more than a few words; use sparingly, one of the more novelty-leaning faces in this set.

fonts.name: Source Serif 4
fonts.description: Adobe's companion serif to Source Sans — even, restrained, built for long-form reading; already our own résumé/cover-letter face, quiet rather than decorative.
fonts.avoid_for: Display headlines — it was drawn for paragraphs, not a large wordmark.

fonts.name: Lora
fonts.description: A moderately-contrasted serif with slightly brushed, calligraphic curves; warm and readable in long paragraphs, a common article/blog-body choice.
fonts.avoid_for: Dense tabular résumé data (dates, figures) — its proportional numerals aren't built for column alignment.

fonts.name: PT Serif
fonts.description: A sturdy transitional serif originally designed for Cyrillic/Latin coexistence; plain, a touch heavier than Lora, reads dependable rather than literary.
fonts.avoid_for: A headline or hero moment — only regular and bold ship, no light or expressive weight to lean into.

fonts.name: Noto Serif
fonts.description: Google's pan-Unicode serif — deliberately neutral, drawn to look consistent across every script it covers; safe and legible but the least 'designed' of the serifs in this set.
fonts.avoid_for: A moment that wants personality (marketing, a wordmark) — it was drawn for universal coverage, not character.

fonts.name: Crimson Pro
fonts.description: A book-typography serif in the Garamond/Caslon old-style tradition; classic and literary at body-text sizes, comfortable for a long résumé or cover letter read.
fonts.avoid_for: UI chrome or small labels — its delicate serifs blur at very small sizes on lower-density screens.

fonts.name: Spectral
fonts.description: A serif drawn specifically for on-screen reading comfort (originally for WordPress); slightly heavier and more even than Crimson Pro, reads well on a laptop the way a résumé actually gets read.
fonts.avoid_for: Print-first documents wanting a higher-contrast, traditional-press serif — Spectral was tuned for the screen, not the page.

fonts.name: Literata
fonts.description: Google's ebook-reading serif (built for Play Books); a wide optical-size range, comfortable and warm at long-form reading sizes with real weight range for emphasis.
fonts.avoid_for: A short marketing headline — its personality is calm and bookish, not a punchy display moment.

fonts.name: Bitter
fonts.description: A slab serif with squared, confident serifs; sturdier and more structured-looking than the other document serifs here, gives a résumé a more assertive, organized feel.
fonts.avoid_for: A delicate or literary tone — the slab reads structured and technical, not warm.

fonts.name: JetBrains Mono
fonts.description: A mono drawn for code, with a tall x-height and easily distinguished 0/O and 1/l/I; already our tool-output and file-path face, calm and legible at small sizes.
fonts.avoid_for: Nothing in this library specifically — note the app today pins the static @fontsource/jetbrains-mono package at 400/500 rather than the variable one; switch packages deliberately, not by accident, if a smoother weight range is ever needed.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Mono
fonts.description: IBM Plex's mono companion — slightly narrower and more geometric than JetBrains Mono, pairs naturally with IBM Plex Sans for a cohesive technical UI.
fonts.avoid_for: Mixing with a very different body sans — its proportions were drawn as part of the Plex family and look most at home there.

fonts.name: Space Mono
fonts.description: A quirky, slightly retro monospace with distinctive rounded terminals; more a designed object than a neutral code font — good for a single stat or number callout, less good for a wall of text.
fonts.avoid_for: Long tool-output blocks — the personality gets tiring at volume; better as a small accent than a body mono.

fonts.name: Fira Code
fonts.description: A code-editor mono with optional ligatures (rendered only where the ligature feature is explicitly enabled); otherwise a clean, even mono close to Fira Sans's own proportions.
fonts.avoid_for: Anywhere ligatures would misrepresent literal tool output or JSON-like text — set font-variant-ligatures: none for anything that must show exact characters.
